L339@P8: on an integrated basis, including identifying the transmission facilities required to provide the

L341@P8: Load and the facilities required for the proposed interconnection of the Proposed Flagship
L342@P8: Generation Facilities.44 PJM will assess whether the transmission facilities identified by AEP Ohio
L343@P8: are sufficient to support the requested level of NITS for the identified load and Capacity
L344@P8: Interconnection Rights (“CIRs”) for the identified generation and, if not, identify any additional
L345@P8: facilities needed to implement the Flagship Project.45 That evaluation will consider the
L346@P8: transmission system as a whole and will test the proposed facilities under the operating conditions

L390@P10: 1. Study Scope and Applicable Criteria
L391@P10: Pursuant to the Study Agreement, PJM, as the independent regional transmission planner,
L392@P10: will be responsible for conducting an integrated, holistic technical evaluation of the Flagship
L393@P10: Project’s proposed load, proposed generation, and the transmission facilities already identified by
L394@P10: AEP Ohio to serve the load and interconnect the generation.55 PJM will assess how those
L395@P10: components operate together on the transmission system, whether the identified facilities can
L396@P10: accommodate the requested NITS and CIR levels under the study scenarios described below and,
L397@P10: if not, what additional transmission may be needed, at a planning level, to support the project and
L398@P10: address resulting reliability violations.56 PJM will conduct the studies in conformance with the
L399@P10: applicable provisions of PJM Manuals 14B (PJM Region Transmission Planning Process) and
L400@P10: Manual 14H (New Service Requests Cycle Process), and in accordance with the process set forth
L401@P10: in Schedule C of the Study Agreement.57 PJM will assess compliance with applicable NERC
L402@P10: Reliability Standards, PJM reliability criteria, and individual Transmission Owners’ planning
L403@P10: criteria.58

L405@P10: through the PJM interconnection queue, the Study Agreement does not alter the substantive
L406@P10: reliability standards or planning criteria applicable to PJM’s evaluation of that generation.

L468@P12: 4. Time Period for Acting on Study Results
L469@P12:  The Study Agreement also places a defined time limit on the Parties’ ability to proceed
L470@P12: based on the study results, including any Required Transmission Upgrades.74 Specifically, no later
L471@P12: than 120 days after PJM delivers a final System Upgrade Report, the PUCO must have either
L472@P12: (i) signed an SAA Agreement for submission, which will be submitted for review and acceptance
L473@P12: by this Commission, or (ii) issued an order that clearly and unequivocally binds customers in Ohio
L474@P12: to be responsible for the allocation of all costs of the Required Transmission Upgrades and confirm
L475@P12: that the Flagship Project is consistent with or furthers Ohio’s Public Policy Requirements.75 The
L476@P12: Parties may extend that 120-day period by mutual agreement; absent an extension, the Study
L477@P12: Agreement automatically terminates if PUCO takes neither action within that period.76 The 120-
L478@P12: day period reflects the need for the State of Ohio to act on the study results before changes in
L479@P12: system conditions or planning assumptions could make those results outdated. Because PJM’s
L480@P12: RTEP is ongoing, if PUCO does not act before expiration of the 120-day period, PJM must
L481@P12: determine whether any part of the studies needs to be updated to reflect then-current conditions
L482@P12: before the identified Required Transmission Upgrades can be considered for RTEP inclusion.
